metadata.title: Pattern Recognition: Feature Selection KP03 Hypothesis Tests
metadata.description: Pattern Recognition, Feature Selection unit, KP03 hypothesis tests; guided v1; English self-study; answer first then feedback

scene-root.name: Pattern Recognition: Feature Selection KP03 Hypothesis Tests

scene-u01.name: Pattern Recognition: Feature Selection KP03 Hypothesis Tests

p01-why-title.name: p01-why-title
p01-why-title.text: Examine features one by one: is the mean difference of the two classes real, or luck?

p01-why-ctx.name: p01-why-ctx
p01-why-ctx.text: Example 5.3: one feature, measured 10 times in each class. First see where the values of the two classes fall and what the means are, then use the "fluctuation" as a ruler for the gap.

p01-why-defn.name: p01-why-defn
p01-why-defn.text: Task of a test: for each feature, is the mean gap $\Delta=\bar x-\bar y$ real or luck? Cheaply drop features without evidence

p01-why-rl.name: p01-why-rl
p01-why-rl.text: Fluctuation ruler: one tick = the fluctuation of the mean difference $0.1128$

p01-why-qn.name: p01-why-qn
p01-why-qn.text: Divide the gap by the fluctuation to know whether it is luck: compare it with the "range of luck"; the next pages explain how the fluctuation is computed and how the range is set

p02-hypo-title.name: p02-hypo-title
p02-hypo-title.text: Hypothesis test: if the gap falls inside the "range of luck", keep $H_0$

p02-hypo-ctx.name: p02-hypo-ctx
p02-hypo-ctx.text: Turn "is there evidence for a mean difference?" into a rule: compute a $q$ and see whether it falls in the acceptance region or the critical region.

p02-hypo-hbox.name: p02-hypo-hbox
p02-hypo-hbox.text:
$H_0$: no difference ($\Delta\mu=0$)
$H_1$: a difference ($\Delta\mu\neq0$)
$q$: gap ÷ fluctuation; its distribution is known when $H_0$ holds

p02-hypo-dec.name: p02-hypo-dec
p02-hypo-dec.text:
$-1.96\leq q\leq 1.96$ ⇒ keep $H_0$
No evidence that the mean is not 1.4

p03-z-title.name: p03-z-title
p03-z-title.text: σ known: compute $q$ step by step (textbook Example 5.1)

p03-z-ctx.name: p03-z-ctx
p03-z-ctx.text: The gap divided by the fluctuation of the mean. The formula in each cell is the input of the next; the large chart below places $q$ on the distribution.

p03-z-zcr.name: p03-z-zcr
p03-z-zcr.text: Red tails at both ends: $\alpha=0.05$ in total

p04-t-title.name: p04-t-title
p04-t-title.text: σ must be estimated from the sample: $t$ has thicker tails, so loosen the threshold

p04-t-ctx.name: p04-t-ctx
p04-t-ctx.text: The estimated $\hat\sigma$ also fluctuates, so $q$ produces extreme values more easily; the more samples, the closer to normal.

p04-t-tr1.name: p04-t-tr1
p04-t-tr1.text: Right: two-sided 95% critical value falls with the degrees of freedom

p04-t-ex52.name: p04-t-ex52
p04-t-ex52.text:
Example 5.2 ($N=16$, df $15$, two-sided 97.5%): critical value $2.49$
$1.35\pm2.49\cdot0.0575=[1.207,\ 1.493]$, wider than the $z$ interval

p05-two-title.name: p05-two-title
p05-two-title.text: Mean difference of two classes: divide $\bar x-\bar y$ by its fluctuation (textbook Example 5.3)

p05-two-ctx.name: p05-two-ctx
p05-two-ctx.text: Pool the two variances to estimate $\sigma$; df $(N-1)+(N-1)=2N-2$; compare $q$ on the $t$ distribution with 18 df.

p05-two-c4.name: p05-two-c4
p05-two-c4.text:
Degrees of freedom $2N-2=18$
Critical value $\pm2.10$
$4.254$ outside ⇒ reject $H_0$

p05-two-cvl.name: p05-two-cvl
p05-two-cvl.text: $t$ distribution with 18 df: the distribution of $q$ when $H_0$ holds

p05-two-why.name: p05-two-why
p05-two-why.text:
Why is the denominator $s_z\sqrt{2/N}$?
$\bar x$ and $\bar y$ each fluctuate with variance $\sigma^2/N$; after subtraction the variance is $2\sigma^2/N$.
$\sigma$ is unknown and estimated by pooling the two classes: $(N-1)+(N-1)=2N-2=18$ independent pieces of information, so use the $t$ distribution with $18$ degrees of freedom.

p06-reject-title.name: p06-reject-title
p06-reject-title.text: q = 4.25 falls far inside the critical region: reject $H_0$

p06-reject-pv.name: p06-reject-pv
p06-reject-pv.text:
$p$-value $=0.0005$
(probability that $|q|$ is this large when $H_0$ holds)

p06-reject-ci.name: p06-reject-ci
p06-reject-ci.text:
95% confidence interval of the mean difference $0.48$
$[0.243,\ 0.717]$: does not contain $0$

p07-assume-title.name: p07-assume-title
p07-assume-title.text: When the assumptions fail: switch tools, does the conclusion change?

p07-assume-ctx.name: p07-assume-ctx
p07-assume-ctx.text: The same data of Example 5.3 and three tests with different assumptions; each bar is its $p$-value (log scale, the longer the smaller $p$).

p07-assume-alp.name: p07-assume-alp
p07-assume-alp.text: $\alpha=0.05$: a bar crossing this line ⇒ $p<\alpha$, reject $H_0$

p07-assume-dq.name: p07-assume-dq
p07-assume-dq.text: The $t$ test has assumptions: equal variances, normality, equal sample sizes

p07-assume-lb0.name: p07-assume-lb0
p07-assume-lb0.text:
Pooled $t$ (check the variances with the $F$ test first)
$F=0.894$ is inside $[0.248,\ 4.03]$, so the variances can be treated as equal

p07-assume-lb1.name: p07-assume-lb1
p07-assume-lb1.text:
Welch $t$: does not require equal variances
$q=4.254$, the same as pooled $t$ when sample sizes are equal

p07-assume-lb2.name: p07-assume-lb2
p07-assume-lb2.text:
Mann–Whitney: no normality assumed
No $t$ distribution used

p07-assume-sum.name: p07-assume-sum
p07-assume-sum.text: All three $p$-values lie to the right of the $\alpha$ line (reject $H_0$): the conclusion does not depend on one assumption, a good sign

p08-n-title.name: p08-n-title
p08-n-title.text: The same gap with different sample sizes gives different conclusions

p08-n-ctx.name: p08-n-ctx
p08-n-ctx.text: The true mean difference $0.2$ and $\sigma=0.25$ are fixed; only the samples per class $N$ change.

p08-n-fm.name: p08-n-fm
p08-n-fm.text: $q=\dfrac{0.2}{0.25\sqrt{2/N}}$: the more samples, the smaller the denominator (fluctuation) and the larger $q$; the critical value also falls at the same time

p08-n-cc.name: p08-n-cc
p08-n-cc.text: With the same true gap, only $N=20$ can see it; failing the test may mean the feature is useless or that there are too few samples

p09-overlap-title.name: p09-overlap-title
p09-overlap-title.text: Significant, yet barely separable: small mean difference, many samples

p09-overlap-ctx.name: p09-overlap-ctx
p09-overlap-ctx.text: 500 samples per class (teaching setup, seed 0), with a true mean gap of only $0.2\sigma$.

p09-overlap-au.name: p09-overlap-au
p09-overlap-au.text:
AUC $=0.544$
Only slightly better than random guessing (0.5)

p10-impute-ctx.name: p10-impute-ctx
p10-impute-ctx.text: Class 2 of Example 5.3 is missing 3 values. Analyze directly, or fill in the mean and then analyze?

p10-impute-cls.name: p10-impute-cls
p10-impute-cls.text: Class 2 is missing value 2, 4, 10, leaving 7: mean $3.129$, sample variance $0.0390$

p10-impute-vt.name: p10-impute-vt
p10-impute-vt.text: Sample variance before and after imputation

p10-impute-rt.name: p10-impute-rt
p10-impute-rt.text:
The 3 imputed values are $0$ from the mean, so the sum of squares stays; the denominator $N-1$ goes $6\to9$
$s^2\times\dfrac{6}{9}=\dfrac{2}{3}$: $0.0390\to0.0260$

p10-impute-cc.name: p10-impute-cc
p10-impute-cc.text: On the same data, filling with the mean raises $q$ from $5.59$ to $6.48$: the denominator is artificially shrunk and the feature looks more discriminative

p11-rank-title.name: p11-rank-title
p11-rank-title.text: Three candidate features: compute one $q$ each and decide by $|q|$

p11-rank-ctx.name: p11-rank-ctx
p11-rank-ctx.text: Left: the range of the two classes (blue = class 1, gold = class 2); right: the $|q|$ bars sorted from large to small, the red dashed line is the critical value, keep only if crossed.

p11-rank-lt.name: p11-rank-lt
p11-rank-lt.text: Range of the 10 values per class

p11-rank-thrl.name: p11-rank-thrl
p11-rank-thrl.text: Critical value $2.10$ (18 df): keep only if crossed

p11-rank-rk.name: p11-rank-rk
p11-rank-rk.text: By $|q|$: F3 $4.54$ > F1 $4.25$ > F2 $1.14$ (dropped); the sign only tells which class is larger

p11-rank-wr.name: p11-rank-wr
p11-rank-wr.text: When many features are tested at once, a few pass by luck

p12-practice1-title.name: p12-practice1-title
p12-practice1-title.text: Exercise 1: is the mean of these 8 values 4.8?

p12-practice1-ctx.name: p12-practice1-ctx
p12-practice1-ctx.text: Work it out yourself first, then press Next for feedback; the right chart is the $t$ distribution of $q$ when $H_0$ holds, and the feedback will draw $q$ and the critical value on it.

p12-practice1-q1.name: p12-practice1-q1
p12-practice1-q1.text: Exercise 1: the 8 values of a feature are $5.1,\ 4.9,\ 5.3,\ 5.0,\ 4.7,\ 5.2,\ 4.8,\ 5.0$. Use a $t$ test ($\alpha=0.05$, two-sided) to test whether the mean is $4.8$.

p12-practice1-cap1.name: p12-practice1-cap1
p12-practice1-cap1.text: Data: range of the 8 values (blue bar)

p12-practice1-ad.name: p12-practice1-ad
p12-practice1-ad.text: Green: acceptance region $\pm2.365$ ($7$ df); red at both ends: critical region

p12-practice1-a2.name: p12-practice1-a2
p12-practice1-a2.text:
Degrees of freedom $7$, critical value $\pm2.365$
$2.828>2.365$ ⇒ reject $H_0$ ($p=0.025$)

p13-practice2-title.name: p13-practice2-title
p13-practice2-title.text: Exercise 2: with only 3 per class, can we still reject $H_0$?

p13-practice2-ctx.name: p13-practice2-ctx
p13-practice2-ctx.text: The same mean difference $0.48$ and $s_z=0.2523$, but with $N=3$ per class.

p13-practice2-q2.name: p13-practice2-q2
p13-practice2-q2.text: Exercise 2: keep $s_z=0.2523$ and the mean difference $0.48$ of Example 5.3, but with only $N=3$ per class. What is $q$? Can we reject $H_0$?

p13-practice2-a2.name: p13-practice2-a2
p13-practice2-a2.text:
$2.33<2.776$: inside the acceptance region
Cannot reject $H_0$

p13-practice2-cmp.name: p13-practice2-cmp
p13-practice2-cmp.text: Example 5.3: with $N=10$, $q=4.25$ can reject; with $N=3$ it cannot: too few samples, large fluctuation, the difference cannot be seen

p14-summary-title.name: p14-summary-title
p14-summary-title.text: The whole KP03: the gap divided by the fluctuation is evidence; significant is not separable

p14-summary-ctx.name: p14-summary-ctx
p14-summary-ctx.text: Each bar = the $|q|$ of a case ÷ critical value; reject $H_0$ only when it crosses 1 time (brackets are page numbers); the last step is the question the next KP answers.

p14-summary-hr.name: p14-summary-hr
p14-summary-hr.text: Critical region: reject $H_0$ ($q$ exceeds the critical value)

p14-summary-axc.name: p14-summary-axc
p14-summary-axc.text: $|q|$ ÷ critical value (1 time = the critical value)

p14-summary-next.name: p14-summary-next
p14-summary-next.text:
The next KP asks: the mean difference is significant, yet the two classes can blur together;
how much do the two classes overlap? ⇒ measure overlap with the ROC curve and AUC

p01-why-nav.name: p01-why-nav
p01-why-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 01/14 · 1 Motivation · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p01-why-cue0.name: p01-why-cue0
p01-why-cue0.text: Look at the definition and the number line first: what does the test answer?

p01-why-cue1.name: p01-why-cue1
p01-why-cue1.text: Look at class 1: the range of its 10 values (bar), the mean (diamond) and the formula.

p01-why-cue2.name: p01-why-cue2
p01-why-cue2.text: Look at class 2: the same feature, the range and mean of the other class.

p01-why-cue3.name: p01-why-cue3
p01-why-cue3.text: Look at the dashed line and the purple pill: how large is the difference of the two means?

p01-why-cue4.name: p01-why-cue4
p01-why-cue4.text: Look at the purple ruler below: measure the mean difference with one fluctuation as the unit.

p01-why-cue5.name: p01-why-cue5
p01-why-cue5.text: Look at the purple box: is a gap alone enough?

p02-hypo-nav.name: p02-hypo-nav
p02-hypo-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 02/14 · 2 Hypothesis test · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p02-hypo-cue0.name: p02-hypo-cue0
p02-hypo-cue0.text: Look at the curve of $q$ first: when $H_0$ holds, $q$ mostly falls in the middle.

p02-hypo-cue1.name: p02-hypo-cue1
p02-hypo-cue1.text: Look at the grey box at the upper left: what are the two hypotheses and $q$?

p02-hypo-cue2.name: p02-hypo-cue2
p02-hypo-cue2.text: Look at the green region: the acceptance region $D$.

p02-hypo-cue3.name: p02-hypo-cue3
p02-hypo-cue3.text: Look at the small red tails at both ends: the critical region.

p02-hypo-cue4.name: p02-hypo-cue4
p02-hypo-cue4.text: Look at the blue line: where does the $q$ computed from the data of Example 5.1 fall?

p03-z-nav.name: p03-z-nav
p03-z-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 03/14 · 3 z test · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p03-z-cue0.name: p03-z-cue0
p03-z-cue0.text: Look at the first cell: which numbers are given? Below is the distribution of $q$.

p03-z-cue1.name: p03-z-cue1
p03-z-cue1.text: Look at the second cell: how much does the mean itself fluctuate?

p03-z-cue2.name: p03-z-cue2
p03-z-cue2.text: Look at the third cell: how large is the observed gap?

p03-z-cue3.name: p03-z-cue3
p03-z-cue3.text: Look at the fourth cell: the gap divided by the fluctuation; the blue line is the position of $q$ on the distribution.

p03-z-cue4.name: p03-z-cue4
p03-z-cue4.text: Look at the fifth cell and the green region: which stretch is the acceptance region?

p03-z-cue5.name: p03-z-cue5
p03-z-cue5.text: Look at the red tails at both ends: $q$ did not reach them.

p04-t-nav.name: p04-t-nav
p04-t-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 04/14 · 3 t test · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p04-t-cue0.name: p04-t-cue0
p04-t-cue0.text: Look at the two axes first: the curves on the left and the critical values on the right.

p04-t-cue1.name: p04-t-cue1
p04-t-cue1.text: Look at the black normal curve and the blue $t$ (15 degrees of freedom).

p04-t-cue2.name: p04-t-cue2
p04-t-cue2.text: Then look at the red $t$ (2 degrees of freedom): the tails are much higher.

p04-t-cue3.name: p04-t-cue3
p04-t-cue3.text: Look at the blue line on the right: how does the critical value change with the degrees of freedom?

p04-t-cue4.name: p04-t-cue4
p04-t-cue4.text: Look at the dashed line: with large degrees of freedom it approaches the normal 1.96.

p04-t-cue5.name: p04-t-cue5
p04-t-cue5.text: Look at the gold box: the confidence interval computed with $t$.

p05-two-nav.name: p05-two-nav
p05-two-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 05/14 · 3 Two-class t · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p05-two-cue0.name: p05-two-cue0
p05-two-cue0.text: Look at the first cell: which statistics does each class have? Below is the $t$ distribution with 18 df.

p05-two-cue1.name: p05-two-cue1
p05-two-cue1.text: Look at the second cell: pool the variances of the two classes.

p05-two-cue2.name: p05-two-cue2
p05-two-cue2.text: Look at the third cell: the fluctuation of the mean difference itself.

p05-two-cue3.name: p05-two-cue3
p05-two-cue3.text: Look at the fourth cell: gap divided by fluctuation; the blue line is the position of $q$ on the distribution.

p05-two-cue4.name: p05-two-cue4
p05-two-cue4.text: Look at the fifth cell and the green region: the critical values $\pm2.10$ enclose the acceptance region.

p05-two-cue5.name: p05-two-cue5
p05-two-cue5.text: Look at the red critical regions at both ends: where does $q$ fall?

p05-two-cue6.name: p05-two-cue6
p05-two-cue6.text: Look at the grey box on the left: why does the denominator look like this?

p06-reject-nav.name: p06-reject-nav
p06-reject-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 06/14 · 3 Two-class t · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p06-reject-cue0.name: p06-reject-cue0
p06-reject-cue0.text: Look at the distribution curve first: the $t$ with 18 degrees of freedom.

p06-reject-cue1.name: p06-reject-cue1
p06-reject-cue1.text: Look at the green acceptance region: between $\pm2.10$.

p06-reject-cue2.name: p06-reject-cue2
p06-reject-cue2.text: Look at the red critical regions at both ends.

p06-reject-cue3.name: p06-reject-cue3
p06-reject-cue3.text: Look at the blue line: where is $q=4.254$?

p06-reject-cue4.name: p06-reject-cue4
p06-reject-cue4.text: Look at the two boxes at the upper left: the $p$-value and the confidence interval say the same thing.

p07-assume-nav.name: p07-assume-nav
p07-assume-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 07/14 · 4 Assumptions and tools · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p07-assume-cue0.name: p07-assume-cue0
p07-assume-cue0.text: Look at this ruler first: a bar crossing the red dashed line ($\alpha=0.05$) rejects $H_0$.

p07-assume-cue1.name: p07-assume-cue1
p07-assume-cue1.text: Look at the first bar: are the variances equal? Check with the $F$ test, then use pooled $t$.

p07-assume-cue2.name: p07-assume-cue2
p07-assume-cue2.text: Look at the second bar: Welch, which does not require equal variances.

p07-assume-cue3.name: p07-assume-cue3
p07-assume-cue3.text: Look at the third bar: Mann–Whitney, which does not assume normality.

p07-assume-cue4.name: p07-assume-cue4
p07-assume-cue4.text: Look at the gold star: what do the three bars say together?

p08-n-nav.name: p08-n-nav
p08-n-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 08/14 · 5 Sample size · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p08-n-cue0.name: p08-n-cue0
p08-n-cue0.text: Look at the formula and axes first: which quantities change when the sample size $N$ changes?

p08-n-cue1.name: p08-n-cue1
p08-n-cue1.text: Look at the bar for $N=3$ and the red dashed line (critical value); the thin line between them is their difference.

p08-n-cue2.name: p08-n-cue2
p08-n-cue2.text: Look at the bar for $N=5$ and the red dashed line (critical value); the thin line between them is their difference.

p08-n-cue3.name: p08-n-cue3
p08-n-cue3.text: Look at the bar for $N=10$ and the red dashed line (critical value); the thin line between them is their difference.

p08-n-cue4.name: p08-n-cue4
p08-n-cue4.text: Look at the bar for $N=20$ and the red dashed line (critical value); the thin line between them is their difference.

p08-n-cue5.name: p08-n-cue5
p08-n-cue5.text: Look at the gold star: does failing the test always mean the feature is useless?

p09-overlap-nav.name: p09-overlap-nav
p09-overlap-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 09/14 · 5 Significant is not separable · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p09-overlap-cue0.name: p09-overlap-cue0
p09-overlap-cue0.text: Look at the horizontal axis first: the feature value, one unit per tick.

p09-overlap-cue1.name: p09-overlap-cue1
p09-overlap-cue1.text: Look at the two coloured areas: the distributions of 500 samples per class.

p09-overlap-cue2.name: p09-overlap-cue2
p09-overlap-cue2.text: Look at the two vertical lines: the means of the two classes.

p09-overlap-cue3.name: p09-overlap-cue3

p09-overlap-cue4.name: p09-overlap-cue4

p10-impute-nav.name: p10-impute-nav
p10-impute-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 10/14 · 5 Consequence of preprocessing · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p10-impute-cue0.name: p10-impute-cue0

p10-impute-cue1.name: p10-impute-cue1

p10-impute-cue2.name: p10-impute-cue2

p10-impute-cue3.name: p10-impute-cue3

p10-impute-cue5.name: p10-impute-cue5

p11-rank-nav.name: p11-rank-nav
p11-rank-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 11/14 · 6 Decide · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p11-rank-cue0.name: p11-rank-cue0
p11-rank-cue0.text: Look at the two axes first: the range of the two classes on the left, $|q|$ on the right, and the red dashed line is the critical value.

p11-rank-cue1.name: p11-rank-cue1
p11-rank-cue1.text: Look at rank 1 F3: the range of the two classes, the $|q|$ bar and the decision.

p11-rank-cue2.name: p11-rank-cue2

p11-rank-cue3.name: p11-rank-cue3

p12-practice1-nav.name: p12-practice1-nav
p12-practice1-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Feature selection · KP03 · 12/14 · Exercise · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; answer first, then reveal

p12-practice1-cue0.name: p12-practice1-cue0
